title: Lee Resolution: Steps to Independence
learningObjectives: Sequence key steps from the 1775 Continental Congress meeting through the Lee Resolution and follow-up actions in 1776-1777.
Order the introduction of the independence resolution, appointment of committees, and adoption of independence measures.

evidence.quote: proposing independence for the American colonies.
a declaration of independence, a call to form foreign alliances,

explanations.text: The resolution proposed independence for the colonies and contained three parts including a declaration and a call for alliances.

evidence.quote: the Congress appointed three concurrent committees in response to the Lee Resolution
one to draft a declaration of independence

explanations.text: Congress responded to the resolution by appointing three committees to handle independence, alliances, and confederation.

evidence.quote: New York cast no vote until the newly elected New York Convention upheld the Declaration of Independence on July 9, 1776.
The plan for making treaties was not approved until September of 1776; the plan of confederation was delayed until November of 1777.

explanations.text: New York did not vote at first but later upheld independence, while the treaty and confederation plans were approved in later months.

evidence.quote: Its second meeting convened in Philadelphia in 1775.

events.label: Second Continental Congress convenes in Philadelphia

evidence.quote: On June 7, 1776, Richard Henry Lee of Virginia, introduced this resolution
proposing independence for the American colonies.
On June 11, 1776, the Congress appointed three concurrent committees in response to the Lee Resolution
one to draft a declaration of independence
On that date, Congress adopted the first part (the declaration).
